title: Conformational Dynamics and Ligand Binding Kinetics of New Delhi Metallo-beta-Lactamase-1 (NDM-1): A Combined Conventional Molecular Dynamics and Ligand Gaussian Accelerated Molecular Dynamics (LiGaMD) Simulation Study.
authors: Shamshad, Sharoon; Ahmed, Ayaz; Moin, Syed Tarique
journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
one_liner_zh: 该文结合常规MD和LiGaMD模拟研究NDM-1与抑制剂复合物的构象动态和结合动力学，属于蛋白质结构相关的计算模拟研究，方法创新且直接服务于抑制剂设计。
abstract: New Delhi metallo-beta-lactamase-1 (NDM-1) is an enzyme responsible for antimicrobial resistance against all major classes of antibiotics, posing a serious health threat to worldwide healthcare systems. Understanding its structural and dynamical properties due to ligand binding will be helpful in pursuing the development of effective inhibitors. For these purposes, conventional molecular dynamics simulations have been successfully applied to evaluate the structural and dynamical properties of free NDM-1 and its three distinct complexes with SFC, SPC, and CAP inhibitors in terms of root mean square deviation (RMSD), root mean square fluctuation (RMSF), MM-PBSA-based free energy, protein-ligand interaction fingerprints, and ligand network analysis. Comparative analyses have also been performed to characterize changes in the conformational landscape of NDM-1 due to inhibitor binding, as a distant loop L7, was observed to be perturbed by the Zn-binding residue His-165, thus suggesting a potential allosteric site. Furthermore, LiGaMD simulations have been applied to these three complexes in the form of a replica that enabled sampling of rare conformational states and provided insights into ligand binding and unbinding kinetics. Based on LiGaMD simulations, the loop L7 was also highlighted as a transiently accessible binding region; however, further investigation was essentially required to establish this site as a potential binding site. Among these complexes, the SFC/NDM-1 complex was found to be the most optimal one, as deduced based on the most favorable balance of binding thermodynamics and kinetics, suggesting its further evaluation to establish it as a lead scaffold. These findings from the study, therefore, provide a detailed understanding of the mechanistic and kinetic features of NDM-1 and may be implicated in the rational design of novel inhibitors targeting the clinically significant NDM-1 enzyme responsible for broad antibiotic resistance.
abstract_zh: 新德里金属-β-内酰胺酶-1（NDM-1）是一种导致对所有主要类别抗生素产生抗药性的酶，对全球医疗系统构成严重健康威胁。理解配体结合引起的其结构和动力学特性，将有助于推动有效抑制剂的开发。为此，常规分子动力学（molecular dynamics）模拟已成功应用于评估游离NDM-1及其与SFC、SPC和CAP抑制剂形成的三种不同复合物的结构和动力学特性，包括均方根偏差（RMSD）、均方根波动（RMSF）、基于MM-PBSA的自由能、蛋白质-配体相互作用指纹图谱以及配体网络分析。还进行了比较分析，以表征抑制剂结合引起的NDM-1构象景观变化，观察到远端环L7受到锌结合残基His-165的扰动，从而提示一个潜在别构位点。此外，LiGaMD模拟以复制品形式应用于这三种复合物，能够采样稀有构象状态，并提供配体结合和解离动力学的见解。基于LiGaMD模拟，环L7也被强调为瞬时可及的结合区域；然而，需要进一步研究以确定该位点作为潜在结合位点。在这些复合物中，SFC/NDM-1复合物被发现是最优的，这是基于结合热力学和动力学最有利的平衡推断得出的，建议进一步评估以将其确立为先导骨架。因此，本研究的发现提供了对NDM-1机制和动力学特征的详细理解，并可能应用于针对临床上重要的NDM-1酶（负责广泛抗生素耐药性）的新型抑制剂的合理设计。
